title: Gangnam Dream
description:
Three billion won.
The deed to a Gangnam apartment, in his hand.

Five years ago, there were nights in a goshiwon room, buried under a blanket, staring at a phone screen at dawn.
Gangnam — three billion. A number so big it was almost funny.

Now {name} stands in that living room, the city laid out below the big window.

The doorbell rings. It's his father.
He opens the door. Hands worn from a lifetime in a factory, shoulders bent.

His father came into the living room and stared out the window for a long while.
He didn't say a word. Just looked.

Then, quietly, he said.
"...It's good, son."

{name} couldn't say anything.
Six years of debt and five years of struggle were all packed into those few words.

The two of them stood side by side, looking at Gangnam at night.

It wasn't winning.
He just — hadn't lost.

description_if_known.used_daeun_as_means:
Three billion.
The deed to a Gangnam apartment, in his hands. With Daeun.

A three-bedroom. Daeun still at his side.
A home with rooms for both their parents — on the surface, the home of a man who came the warm way.

But {name} knows. There was a night he turned her name into a document.
Daeun never asked; {name} never told. That silence still lived somewhere in this home.

He got Gangnam, and Daeun is beside him.
Only — there was a hairline crack in the perfectly clean glass, visible to {name} alone.
Happy, and yet that crack caught the light differently, now and then.
description_if_known.daeun_married:
Three billion.
The deed to a Gangnam apartment, in his hands. With Daeun.

A three-bedroom. The big room for the two of them, one small room for his father, one for Daeun's mother when she comes up to Seoul.
The number that was 'my deed' five years ago — became a home with rooms for both their parents.

The doorbell rings. His father. Hands that worked a factory floor a lifetime, stooped shoulders.
Daeun runs out first and opens the door. "Father!"

His father comes into the living room and looks out the window. It was Gangnam.
This time he wasn't alone. A daughter-in-law at his side, his son's hand in his.

{name} took Daeun's hand. At least he had made it here without putting her name on the paperwork for a shortcut.
Gangnam had been the destination. Once here, the first thing to fill was not the rooms, but the seats for people.
description_if_known.jiyeon_romance_started:
Three billion.
The deed to a Gangnam apartment, in his hands. With Han Jiyeon.

At her family's, his father-in-law now accepts {name} as a true son-in-law. "My eye was never wrong."
The man who stood on tiptoe at the threshold of her world five years ago — now stands in it on both feet.

Jiyeon took his arm. "See? This is who you were all along, oppa."

{name} smiled. Becoming the man she wanted — whether that was pride, or fitting himself to her standard.
Before the Gangnam night, the line between them blurred. Only today — he stood on the winning side.

The deed to a Gangnam apartment, in his hands.

He stands in that living room now, the city spread below the wide window.

The doorbell rings. His father.
He opens the door. Hands that worked a factory floor for a lifetime, shoulders bent.

His father came into the living room and looked out the window for a long time.
Then said, quietly,
"...It's good. Son."

{name} thought of Im Sangchul.
The day he said he forgave him. And months later, the day he asked himself whether he'd meant it.
Both times, the same answer.

The forgiveness was never for that man.
The road was simply too long to climb carrying hatred.

The two of them stood side by side, looking at the Gangnam night.
He never knew empty hands could feel this light.

Somewhere in those lights, that man is out there too.
No hatred. Only memory.

description_if_known.jaehyuk_stood_up:
Gangnam.

I thought of the year Jaehyuk disappeared. I'd put everything in. He vanished.
Rock bottom. Real rock bottom.

Built again from there. Not his way.

{name} made it to Gangnam — but {name} was the one who made the trip.
The road was longer. Slower. And more {name}'s own for it.

Called Dad. He picked up. Couldn't find words.

Gangnam. Here. That's all.
And somehow — that was enough.
description_if_known.year4_final_resolve:
Three billion won.
The Gangnam apartment title deed is in hand.

Standing in that living room now, the city spread out below through a wide window.

A year ago, there was a resolution.
The last year. Would remember this feeling.

{name} remembered it.

Gangnam. Made it.
What was decided became real.

Called Dad. Connected.

title: Empty House
description:
A Gangnam apartment.
{name}'s name is printed on the deed.

He reached the goal.

But there is no one to show it to.

Last winter, his father slipped away quietly while hospitalized.
The call when he'd said, 'I'll definitely come down next month' — was the last.

A wide living room. A big window. A night view with no one in it.
There were two mugs on the table. One was still dry.

{name} put the deed back in its envelope and pulled the second mug toward himself.
He had wanted to show his father.
That had been the real reason from the start.

In the place where that reason should be sitting — a three-billion-won home.

description_if_known.father_reconciled:
A Gangnam apartment.
{name}'s name is printed on the deed.

There were two mugs on the table. The last time his father came to Seoul, they had sat in those same places.

Their calls after reconciling were surprisingly ordinary. Did you eat, how is your knee, next time I'll buy the gukbap. Even the last call ended with words like those, not an apology.

{name} filled the second mug with water, then set it down without drinking.

A home he never got to show him.
But not a home left behind by two people who had kept pretending not to know each other.

Gangnam's lights rested side by side in the two mugs.
description_if_known.father_confession_heard:
A Gangnam apartment.
In the envelope beside the deed was a page with the name and case number his father had finally spoken aloud.

Before he died, his father told him the truth: whom he trusted, where he signed, and why he could never look his son in the eye afterward.
{name} heard all of it. Too late, but not never.

There were two mugs on the table. One seat was empty. The envelope lay close to it.

Three billion won could not return his father's years of silence.
But the person hidden inside that silence had come all the way into this home.
description_if_known.promise_reaffirmed:
A Gangnam apartment.
One room had been left empty. Ever since he said he would bring his father here, it was the first room he counted on every floor plan.

He did not keep the promise. Time closed before the house opened.

{name} left the empty room's door open and returned to the living room.
Two mugs on the table. One deed beside them.

The goal arrived before the deadline.
The promise made to a person did not.

Gangnam's night light reached all the way across the empty floor.

title: With Daeun
description:
He didn't make it to Gangnam.

But he has Daeun.

A rented villa on the outskirts. The two of them barely getting by on what they earn.
On weekends they boil ramyeon, just like that first time they met at the convenience store.

Daeun picks up her chopsticks and asks.
"Do you regret not making it to Gangnam?"

{name} thought for a moment.
The overtime, the failed investments, the goshiwon fridge, all of it.

"I don't know. But right now — I'm not unhappy."

Daeun smiles.

Gangnam was the destination.
But maybe it was a destination he'd set when he didn't yet know what he really wanted.

The ramyeon was going cold. Neither of them ate. It was okay.

description_if_known.daeun_married:
He didn't make it to Gangnam.

Instead, he ended the five years married to Daeun.

The wedding was small. Only as much as the two of them wanted.
They each took one key to a small home on the outskirts.
The woman who had handed him triangle kimbap across a convenience-store counter five years ago — now opened the same door.

On a weekend evening, the ramyeon cooled on their table.
Daeun lifted her chopsticks with her ringed hand and asked,
"Do you regret not making it to Gangnam?"

{name} took that hand.
"I don't know. But right now, I'm not unhappy."

Five years that began as a number ended with the person looking out the same window beside him.
There was no Gangnam. There was a hand he had not let go.
description_if_known.daeun_final_together:
He didn't make it to Gangnam.

Instead, there is Daeun.

A monthly-rent villa on the city's edge. Two incomes, just enough.
On weekends they cook ramyeon, the way it was when they first met at the convenience store.

Daeun picks up her chopsticks and asks,
"Do you regret not making it to Gangnam?"

{name} thought of that last dinner. The rolled omelette.
"We got here together. Without you I'd have folded halfway."
It was true that night, and it was true now.

"I don't know. But right now — I'm not unhappy."

Daeun smiles.

Gangnam was a destination.
But maybe it was the kind you set before you know what you really want.

The ramyeon was going cold. Neither of them ate. It was fine.

title: Jiyeon's Man
description:
He lives in Gangnam. In Han Jiyeon's Gangnam.

A good car, a good house, good people.
At her family's place, his father-in-law now calls {name} 'our son-in-law.'

One night, he stood alone in front of the bathroom mirror.

The man who rode a bicycle around the goshiwon five years ago.
The man who made a triangle kimbap his dinner.
Whether that man and {name} now are the same person — he doesn't know.

He lives in Gangnam.
But whether this is the Gangnam he wanted,
or whether he just moved into the Gangnam Jiyeon already lived in —

Jiyeon knocks on the bathroom door. "Still awake, oppa?"
"Yeah. Still awake."

The door opens. She stands beside him. The two of them reflected in the mirror.

{name} smiled.
A happy smile, but one with something hollow in it.

description_if_known.jiyeon_stayed_as_selves:
Gangnam never came. Han Jiyeon stayed.

She didn't go back to her father's world, and {name} didn't become someone else.
The couple lives in a house that isn't large. Small by her standards, spacious by his.

One dawn, {name} woke and looked again at an old text on his phone.
"Am I kind of strange?"
Beside him Jiyeon stirred awake. "...What are you looking at, oppa?"
"Nothing."
Two strange people live on, believing each other not strange.
And that's enough — both of them, honestly, believe it is.

To hold on to her, {name} became a man of her world. Her father's business, that world's rules, things he never used to do.

One night, he stood alone before the bathroom mirror.
The man who rode a bicycle around the goshiwon five years ago. Who made a triangle kimbap his dinner.
Whether that man and {name} now are the same — he knows now that they aren't.

Jiyeon is beside him. The marriage held.
Only, the man she says she loves is no longer {name}.
description_if_known.jiyeon_gangnam_together:
He lives in Gangnam. In Han Jiyeon's Gangnam.

"See you in Gangnam, oppa" — that had been a promise. When neither of them was there yet.

He stood alone in front of the bathroom mirror one night. The man who rode a bicycle from a goshiwon. The man who ate triangle kimbap for dinner.

Jiyeon knocks on the door. "Still awake, oppa?"
"Yeah. Still awake."

The door opens. In the mirror: both of them.

That promise made before they were there — completed right here.
description_if_known.told_jiyeon_about_records:
He lives in Gangnam.

Jiyeon was already there. For different reasons, by a different road.

Between them there was one thing that no longer needed saying.
HanPD Construction. The name in his father's records.
Minjun had said it, Jiyeon had heard it — and even then, neither of them turned away.

"You made it, oppa."
"I did."

Two people who knew where the other came from, standing in the same city.

Jiyeon smiled. A smile that suited the city.
{name} smiled too. Not a Gangnam entered with questions unasked — a Gangnam chosen with everything known.

title: Jaehyuk's Way
description:
He made it to Gangnam. Fast. Dirty.

He sold other people's information, exploited rivals' weaknesses,
broke promises more times than he could count.

The house he bought with that money.

He invited his father. His father was delighted.
"Wow, amazing. My son."

{name} couldn't smile at those words.

Because the faces he'd trampled on the way up
seemed to be standing right behind his father.

The people he'd hated so much.
And himself, now.

A villa on the outskirts of Seoul. Rent 580,000 a month.
One room with one window, and beyond the window, the wall of the next building.

An ordinary job. An ordinary today.
Subway in the morning, subway in the evening, home to wash up and sleep.

Sometimes when Gangnam apartment prices come up on the news, he blanks out for a second.
'If I'd done things differently.' That thought comes too, sometimes.

But dinner tasted good tonight.
A cup ramyeon bought at the convenience store on the way home.
Rain falling outside, and it's his own room.

{name} went to search something on his phone, then just set it down.

In Seoul, there are far more people who didn't make it to Gangnam than people who did.
{name} is one of them.

Whether that's failure — he doesn't know.
What's certain is that tonight isn't cold.
There are nights when that's enough.

When the five years ended, the balance was still short of three billion won.

He opened the delivery app, then closed it.
Eating alone felt like more trouble than hunger was worth.

No Daeun. No Gangnam.
Only the choice he'd believed could trade one for the other.

Sometimes he remembers what she said as she left. "You're a good person. You're just not from my world."

She was right. {name} stayed in his own world.
Small, but a self traded for nothing. Whether that's losing or winning — he doesn't know.

title: Collapsed from Overwork
description:
His body stopped first.

It happened on the stairs as he was leaving home. Before he made it down a single floor,
he couldn't stay standing without gripping the railing.

There had been signs. Less sleep, skipped meals,
the room spinning every time he went to the bathroom.
Still he didn't stop. Seoul doesn't wait for people who rest.

An ER IV drip. Fluorescent lights on the ceiling.
Someone groaning in the next bed.

A nurse checked the chart and asked,
"Is there someone we can call?"

{name} couldn't answer.
There were people he could call, but they were people he didn't want to call.
Father, mother, army buddies.
He didn't want to worry them. He hadn't achieved anything yet.

Gangnam was the goal.
Somewhere in the running, he lost the person who was running.

Staring at the hospital ceiling, he asked for the first time.

Am I happy right now?

No answer came.
Maybe he'd been the one refusing to let it.

title: Mental Collapse
description:
The psychiatrist's office was quieter than he'd expected.

He held out three weeks before making the appointment.
He hated going outside. He hated people.
At some point, getting out of bed began to use all the energy he had.

The doctor asked, "What feels hardest these days?"

{name} thought for a moment.
He could not say, 'I am not getting to Gangnam.'
It no longer sounded like the actual problem.

"I don't know. Everything feels like too much."

Comparing himself to others had exhausted him. Exhaustion had become collapse before he noticed the fall.
He had believed Seoul pushed the weak aside first.

The doctor made no judgment. She wrote down the next appointment date.
{name} accepted the slip with both hands.

He had not arrived in Gangnam today.
But for the first time, he had an address to reach before he fell apart.

A short breath crossed the line.
"Good. I'm glad you went."

But there was one call that could hold even a weak voice.

For today, he decided to write down only that.

title: Debt Abyss
description:
The day his net worth fell past negative 100 million won, {name} decided to stop looking at the numbers.

At first, the red was small.
He thought it would only be for a moment.
He borrowed more to cover that moment, then risked more to win back the loss.

Leverage magnifies gains.
It magnifies losses by the same factor.
His mind knew. His hands kept moving.

When the first collection call came, he hung up on the unknown number.
The second time, he answered, then hung up.
The third time, he watched the phone vibrate until it stopped.

He sat in the goshiwon room and worked the calculator.
More was due each month than he could bring in.
However many times he entered it, the answer stayed the same.

{name} took his hand off the calculator.
For tonight, he stopped trying to find the exact point where it had gone wrong.

He went out and bought the cheapest canned coffee at the convenience store.
Afterward, only coins remained in his wallet.

Five hundred thousand won in the bank, at the beginning.
Now his net worth sat below negative 100 million.

Tomorrow would still come.
If he began again, it would start with not losing what remained.

description:

A Gangnam apartment. A table for four.
{name} sat alone at the far end.
Seoul at night was beautiful as ever.

Eating alone felt like more trouble than it was worth.

He opened his contacts.
He couldn't remember the last time he'd texted anyone, 'Have you eaten?'

It wasn't that people left while he chased money.
More precisely, the moments he chose money over people had quietly piled up.

He opened the delivery app again and ordered one meal.
The doorbell rang.
One paper bag landed on the table. The other three chairs were empty.

Loneliness worth three billion won was still just loneliness.

title: Investment Master

Why did I buy? When will I admit I was wrong?

The trades that built the balance were not the ones he called correctly, but the ones where he honored the second sentence.
There were days he bought fear and days he sold greed. When he was wrong, he lost small and turned off the screen.

He had never beaten the market.
He had learned how to survive until it opened again.

But {name} now knew what mattered: not only when to enter, but how to leave when he was wrong. Not how much he could make, but how much he could lose and still judge clearly again.

He had not beaten the market.
He had learned how to survive it.

That eye arrived later than the money in his account, and it would last longer.

Seoul is, in the end, a city made of people.

title: Healthy Retirement

Turning off the screen did not reduce the debt.

He sat in the goshiwon room and worked the calculator.
He borrowed to make a payment, then borrowed again to cover the gap.
Debt produced interest. New debt paid that interest and produced more.

What came in each month could no longer cover both the interest and the cost of living.
It had never been a structure that could last.

{name} turned the calculator face-down.
The phone rang. He did not answer.

He stopped calculating.
Even if he found the exact point where it had gone wrong, the answer would change nothing now.

He went out and bought the cheapest canned coffee at the convenience store.
Afterward, only coins remained in his wallet.

There was a day he accepted the margin call.
That day did not settle a loss. It reserved another round.
Those reservations stacked up into this.

title: Pinnacle of the Orthodox
description:
It was the final grill at a team dinner.
As the smoke thinned, a junior asked,

"How did you last that long?"

{name} had one billion won in the bank. It was not Gangnam.
Pay stubs, the year he was passed over, and the first salary negotiation where he named his own number overlapped inside that amount.

He still did not know whether diligence had kept him there, or fear of every other road.

A piece of meat began to burn. The junior reached for the tongs.
{name} emptied his water glass and said,

"I made it to the next month. Every time."

There was no brighter secret than that.
One billion won sat quietly between them.

Playing it straight didn't mean enduring — it included demanding fairly.

title: Hollow Success
description:
At thirty-eight, he checked his balance in the banking app.

The number was enough.

He stared out the window for a long while. He felt nothing.

He lived diligently. The way society wanted.
Didn't skip overtime, invested safely, didn't do anything that stood out.
Because that was right — no, more precisely, because people said it was right.

He never once asked what he himself wanted.

Is this success.
It's success, alright. Numbers don't lie.

But in this living room, who am I now.
That — there's no answer.

title: My Own Balance
description:
With the laptop closed at one end of the dinner table, {name} drew four boxes in his notebook.

Work. Investing. Side jobs. And one box left blank.

For five years, the first three had traded places every week. When work became urgent, he invested less. When the side job grew, he cut work before he cut sleep.
The thought that he had failed to push any one road all the way followed him for years.

He did not reach Gangnam. He did not break through, and he did not collapse.

{name} wrote dinner in the empty box.
The food had cooled a little. His bag waited on the chair for tomorrow.

A day remained in which money had not filled every box.

description_if_known.sangchul_network_fully_cut:
Balance wasn't just about how much you bring in — it was also about what you refuse to bring in.

Once, he took his hand off that network. When the door opened again, later — he refused again.
The first time was a decision. The second was a confirmation.

Things were slower after that. He still made it this far.

He didn't make it to Gangnam.
There is no unexplainable source in this money.
The question came twice, and the answer was the same both times.

That was {name}'s balance.

title: The Outsider's Victory
description:
Five hundred million won.

At rush hour, the crowd poured toward one exit while {name} stood at the crossing on the other side.
An old jacket instead of a suit. A worn bag and a notebook instead of a briefcase.

The notebook held the day leverage nearly washed him away and the day a failed investment sent him back through the goshiwon door.
He had not chosen this road because no one else took it. He kept looking for another exit because the road everyone took did not feel like his.

The signal changed.
People brushed past him in the same direction.
{name} put the notebook away and walked between them.

The man he had been five years ago would not have believed the balance.
Now he trusted something else more: his ability to stop at the next signal.

title: Early Retirement
description:
The alarm did not go off.

{name} was thirty-eight that morning.
He checked his phone and only then remembered he had not set one the night before.

For now, he was taking time away from work. Thirty-eight was too early to call it retirement, and life was too long to promise he would never commute again.
But with this balance and pace, leaving work for good before fifty had become possible.

His work bag still hung from the chair. Yesterday's shirt lay folded on the table.
Without moving either one, {name} slowly brewed coffee.

Two buses passed outside.
Once, this was the hour when he checked their route numbers first.

{name} took a sip before opening his banking app.
The day's first decision was not to go anywhere yet.

title: The Age of the Creator
description:
The comment notifications wouldn't stop.

One million.
One million subscribers.

The day he uploaded his first video, it had 43 views.
That wasn't embarrassing. He just wanted to film.

That became 10,000, became 100,000, and now it's come this far.

A brand deal contract came in.
An amount more than a month's rent on a Gangnam apartment.

Signing it, {name} had a strange feeling.
Doing what he wanted to do, and the money followed.

He didn't know this kind of way existed five years ago.

There wasn't just one way to survive in Seoul.
{name} standing in front of the camera is the proof.

title: Myth
description:
Five hundred thousand won.
The first year.
Three billion.

It's a number that makes no sense. {name} himself knows it.

Whether it was at the racetrack or in front of a chart — only {name} knows what happened that day.
The odds that day, the bet that day. He could never do it again.

The deed to a Gangnam apartment, in his hand.
It came so fast that none of it feels real.

He still hasn't reconciled with his father.
He still hasn't met the people he was meant to meet.
A whole five years were still left.

And yet it's over. Because he reached the goal.

People will tell this story for years.
'A jobless guy living in a goshiwon made it to Gangnam before his first year was over.'
No one will believe it.

Seoul sometimes allows one impossible thing like this.
Who it'll be — no one knows.

— You found a path that was never designed.
This almost never happens.

title: In His Father's Name
description:
On the day he entered Gangnam, he called his father.
'Dad, that debt to the Im guy — I paid it all off.'
A brief silence.
'...How?'
'From the man himself.'

His father was quiet for a long time, then wept.

Minjun looked out the window. It was Gangnam. The same sky as the day he first arrived.

title: Human Until Gangnam
description:
Three billion won.
The deed to a Gangnam apartment, in hand.

One moving box still sat open in the corner of the living room.
{name} stood at the window with the papers. Gangnam-daero ran far below in the afternoon light.

Five years ago, he had arrived in the same city with five hundred thousand won in his pocket.
There had been many slow days after that. Days he stopped in front of someone else's pace, and days he closed the faster door.

{name} looked at his hand before he looked at the deed.
What came back was not only what the hand had gained, but what it had refused to do.

He opened the box. The old notebook lay on top.
Under 'Three billion. Five years.' on the first page, he wrote today's date.

He did not cross out the sentence. He turned the page.

description_if_known.cleared_father_debt_from_sangchul:
Three billion won.
On the moving box, he placed the deed beside the confirmation that his father's debt had been repaid.

{name} took back what Im Sangchul owed, but he did not use the man's ladder.
The two documents reached the same home without becoming the price of each other.

Afternoon light spread across Gangnam-daero.
{name} slipped the confirmation into the old notebook and turned the page.

The first name he would write today was not his own.
description_if_known.sangchul_quietly_distanced:
Three billion won.
An old business card came out of the open moving box. Im Sangchul.

The calls he did not answer and the rooms he did not enter after leaving that cafe had become five years of empty space.
The road took longer, but nothing in the view required an explanation of that man's hand.

{name} did not throw the card away. He placed it between two closed pages of the notebook.
He kept it to remember, not to carry into the next page.
description_if_known.promise_reaffirmed:
Three billion won.
Still holding the deed, {name} opened the door to the empty small room.

There was a promise he had made to his father on a Sunday-night call: that he would get there, that he would make a place for him.
For five years, that sentence had aged beside the numbers in the notebook.

{name} left the door open and returned to the living room.
He wrote today's date under the first page.
On the day the goal arrived, he left the promised place open first.
description_if_known.kept_clean_hands:
Three billion won.
The first page of the old notebook held one sum he never received.
Two million won for lending out his bank account. A number that never appeared in the balance.

Five years of transactions followed that blank line.
{name} placed the deed beside it and opened his palm.

He did not write that it was clean.
He wrote today's date instead, then turned the page.

title: To Gangnam, Together
description:
From their home across the river, the lights of Gangnam were visible.
Daeun stood by the window and looked out at the night.
"You can see it well from here too."
{name} said, "At first, getting over there was the goal."
Daeun turned around. "And now?"

{name} didn't answer. Instead, he made another cup of coffee.

Even lights they never reached could brighten a home when they looked at them together.

title: The Things He Kept
description:
On the day his father was discharged, Minjun went down to Changwon.

In the hospital parking lot, his father said.
'Don't you have to go back to Seoul?'
'I'll stay a while.'

Minjun carried his father's bags.
There was no Gangnam yet. There was something to do before that.

title: One More Circle
description:
He didn't make it to Gangnam.

The bankbook fell far short of the goal.
The three billion he'd set five years ago remained, in the end, only a number.

But a calendar hangs above {name}'s desk.
The circles kept growing after the first thirty.

Gambling-free days, carried all the way to today.

There was a time {name} hit rock bottom.
Blowing borrowed money, calculating the next hand at dawn.
There, he reached out a hand. Asking for help.

That was the best thing he did in these five years.

In terms of money it may be a lost game.
But not losing himself — that was something three billion couldn't buy.

{name} drew one more circle on the calendar today.
He'll draw one tomorrow too. That's enough.

title: The Ladder He Switched
description:
His business card changed three times.

Five years ago, he started at a convenience store night counter.
Next was an office job, then a bigger company, and now — a place you'd know by name.

Others said holding one position was a virtue.
{name} thought differently. Holding on and being trapped are different things.

The day he named a number first at the salary negotiation table,
the day he listened to the headhunter's call to the end instead of hanging up,
the day his hand didn't tremble as he handed in his resignation.

Those days piled up into his current title.

He couldn't buy a Gangnam apartment. Three billion was far off.
But {name} proved his worth to the market,
and that worth rose every year.

On the way home, he saw his reflection in the building lobby glass.
The suit didn't feel awkward.

He hadn't climbed a ladder.
He'd kept switching to a better one.

title: The Things He Endured
description:
The commuter bus emptied out on the way to the last stop.
{name} rolled up his wet suit sleeve and turned off the phone screen.

He had worked for five years. He searched for another workplace and either moved on or, in the end, stayed.
Even after he first said the word burnout aloud, there were almost no blank days on his attendance record.

Thirty-eight. He still had a job.
Not three billion won. Not even a hundred million.

When the bus stopped, the driver looked at {name} through the mirror.
He rose late and stepped out into the rain.

He would go to work tomorrow.
He had not decided whether that sentence was relief or warning.
For the walk home, he decided not to reach any conclusion.

The bus stopped at the end of the line.

Changing jobs had not been the wrong choice. The pay was better, and the work fit him more.
But there was fatigue inside his body that could not be copied onto a new business card.

{name} rolled up his wet suit sleeve and stepped off the bus.
There had been a time when he thought changing companies would change everything.

The destination changed.
The body getting off the last bus came with him.

Standing in the rain, he found that senior's number.
This time, before asking about the next company, he would ask how the man had learned to rest.

There was one missed call from his father on the phone.

Before, he would have left it until tomorrow. Too tired, nothing to say.
After reconciling, the two of them rarely spoke at length. That made it easier to call now.

{name} stepped off the bus and stood beneath an awning.
"Dad. Are you still awake?"

Through the rain, his father asked whether he had eaten.
He would go to work tomorrow. Tonight, he listened to the end of the call first.

title: Reckoning
description:
He didn't make it to Gangnam.

Instead, he wrote a statement at the police station.
Park Sang-jin. Im Sangchul. The two names that brought down his father six years ago.

The hand writing the statement trembled.
Because he knew that the moment he wrote it, the last ladder to Gangnam would be pulled away.
Im Sangchul's network, the information he provided, those seats — all of it, over.

Still he didn't stop the pen.

He came home and called his father.
"Dad. About that debt. It's not your fault anymore. I looked into all of it."

The other end of the line was quiet for a long time.
And then his father, for the first time in his life, cried like a child.

There was no Gangnam apartment.
But that one phone call let him set down something heavier than six years of debt.

{name} opened the window.
Today, even the sky over Gangnam was just sky.

title: The Chronicler
description:
A story that began at thirty-three, in a goshiwon room.
He didn't reach Gangnam. Not three billion, not an apartment. At thirty-eight, he was still living in a goshiwon.

But one day, he began to write — everything that had happened.

Convenience store lunchboxes and 3 a.m., the first paycheck and the failed villa lease, a friend's wedding invitation and the New Year's rice cake soup eaten alone. The stock charts he pored over through sleepless nights, and the bathroom at the end of the goshiwon hall.

A memoir of a failed Gangnam dream.

First printing 50,000 copies. Number-one bestseller two weeks after release.
